title: The Canadian
sub: The Canadian G&CC · East 9 · White/Front · Par 35 · ~2,950 yds to pins
thesis: Your first visit here was 51, and the whole story was two holes: the S.I.-1 par 5 (#5) and the "steal" that wasn't (#7). Hold those two and this is a mid-40s nine. Everything else, the plan already worked: you bogeyed the 194 forced carry (#2) and PARRED the 125 water carry (#6). One ball, aim dry, advance to a wedge, take the bogey.

keysTitle: Five things to run the East
keys: #5 is the discipline hole. Lay up short of the green water, never go for it. S.I. 1 with water at the green did exactly what it threatened and made an 8. A dry bogey 6 there is a great number.
#7 is a position hole, not a steal. Water runs LEFT and driver brings it in play. Hybrid or 5i off the tee, aim center-right, and it's a routine bogey instead of an ambush 7.
The water-carry par 3s are real now. You parred the 125 (#6) here and bogeyed the 194 (#2). Commit to the carry, aim center, and let the short game clean up.
Smooth is full and committed, not light. "More" gives you a slice right and less distance, and on this nine it feeds the water. If smooth won't reach, club up.
Putts: die it at the hole. 17 putts held up here on greens you'd never seen. Lines are good, speed is the miss. Short putts lean right → aim the LEFT EDGE.
footer: White/Front · Par 35 · target 44 · "last:" from your Jul 25 first visit (51). Both penalties tracked the flagged water on #5 and #7.
